name: System Design Basics
description: Designing scalable, reliable services using load balancing, caching, databases, queues and sensible trade-offs.

questions.question: What is the main job of a load balancer?
options: Encrypting data at rest
Compressing database tables
Storing user sessions permanently
Distributing incoming requests across multiple servers
questions.explanation: Load balancers spread traffic across backends to improve capacity and availability.

questions.question: What does horizontal scaling mean?
options: Adding more machines to share the load
Adding more CPU and RAM to a single machine
Rewriting the service in a faster language
Reducing the number of features
questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling (scale out) adds nodes; vertical scaling (scale up) makes one node bigger.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of placing a cache such as Redis in front of a database?
options: To guarantee strong consistency
To replace backups
To reduce latency and database load by serving frequently read data from memory
To enforce foreign keys
questions.explanation: Caches serve hot data quickly from memory, at the cost of possible staleness that must be managed.

questions.question: According to the CAP theorem, during a network partition a distributed system must choose between:
options: Latency and throughput
Consistency and availability
Durability and partition tolerance
Scalability and security
questions.explanation: When a partition occurs, a system can either reject some requests to stay consistent or keep serving and risk inconsistency.

questions.question: Why place a message queue between an order service and an email-sending service?
options: To make emails send synchronously before responding
To remove the need for retries
To store orders permanently instead of a database
To decouple the services so emails are processed asynchronously and survive temporary consumer outages
questions.explanation: Queues buffer work, absorb traffic spikes and let the consumer fail and retry without blocking order placement.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of consistent hashing for distributing keys across cache nodes?
options: It encrypts keys
It guarantees every node holds exactly the same number of keys
When a node is added or removed, only a small fraction of keys need to move
It eliminates the need for replication
questions.explanation: With modulo hashing nearly all keys remap when node count changes; consistent hashing limits remapping to roughly K/N keys.

practical.title: Sketch a URL shortener
practical.instructions: In 4-6 sentences, describe a design for a URL shortener: how you generate short codes, where you store the mappings, how you handle heavy read traffic, how you scale, and which HTTP status code the redirect returns.
practical.expected_output: Codes from a counter/unique ID encoded in base62 (or a hash); mappings in a key-value store or database; a cache (e.g. Redis/CDN) for hot links; load balancer with replicas or sharding; redirect with 301/302.

rubric.hint: Explain how codes are generated, e.g. base62-encoding an auto-increment ID.
Say where code-to-URL mappings are stored.
Reads dominate; cache popular mappings in memory.
Mention load balancing, read replicas or sharding.

tasks.title: Read the System Design Primer fundamentals
tasks.description: Read the primer sections on performance vs scalability, latency vs throughput, availability vs consistency, DNS, CDNs and load balancers. Summarise each in two sentences.
tasks.completion_criteria: Written summaries for at least 6 core concepts.

tasks.title: Diagram an app you use
tasks.description: Pick a familiar app (e.g. a food-delivery app) and draw its likely architecture: clients, load balancer, services, databases, caches and queues. Label what each component does.
tasks.completion_criteria: A labelled architecture diagram with at least 6 components.

tasks.title: Work through two classic design problems
tasks.description: Design a URL shortener and a news feed using the primer's approach: requirements, capacity estimates, high-level design, then bottlenecks. Compare with the primer's solutions afterwards.
tasks.completion_criteria: Two written designs with capacity estimates and identified trade-offs.

tasks.title: Build and load-test a scaled service
tasks.description: Run a small API behind a load balancer with two instances, a database and a Redis cache using Docker Compose. Load-test it and measure latency with and without caching.
tasks.completion_criteria: Load-test results showing the effect of caching and of running multiple instances.
